title: Chicken and vegetable stir-fry
description: Chicken, broccoli, pepper and carrot tossed in a hot pan with ginger, garlic and soy, over rice.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps.text: Mix the soy sauce, honey, cornstarch and {100 ml} water in a cup until smooth.
steps.tip: Cornstarch sinks, so stir again just before you pour it in.

steps.text: Slice the chicken thinly. Cut the broccoli into small florets, the pepper into strips and the carrots into thin slices. Grate the ginger and garlic.
steps.tip: Have everything cut before you start cooking. A stir-fry moves fast.

steps: Heat {1 tbsp} of the oil in a wok or large frying pan on high until very hot. Stir-fry the chicken for 5 minutes until golden and cooked through, then take it out onto a plate.

steps.text: Add the rest of the oil, then the carrots and broccoli and stir-fry for 2 minutes. Add the pepper, ginger and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes more.
steps.tip: The vegetables should stay bright and a little crunchy. If the broccoli is too firm, add a spoon of water and cover for a moment.

steps: Put the chicken back, pour in the sauce and toss for 1 minute until it bubbles, thickens and turns glossy. Serve with the rice.

title: Thai green chicken curry
description: Chicken and vegetables simmered in coconut milk with green curry paste, lime and a little honey.
steps: Cook the rice. Fry the curry paste in the oil for 1 minute until it smells strong.
Add the sliced chicken and stir until coated, then pour in the coconut milk and 150 ml water.
Add the vegetables in bite-size pieces and simmer 12 minutes.
Season with lime juice, honey and fish sauce. Serve over rice.

title: Chicken teriyaki rice bowls
description: Sticky soy and honey glazed chicken thighs with rice, broccoli and sesame seeds.

ingredients.note: rice vinegar if you have it

steps: Cook the rice and steam the broccoli for 5 minutes.
Mix the soy sauce, honey, vinegar, grated ginger and garlic.
Fry the chicken skin side down in the oil for 8 minutes, turn and cook 6 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce and let it bubble until sticky, turning the chicken. Slice and serve on rice with the broccoli, sesame and spring onion.

title: Salmon teriyaki with cucumber salad
description: Pan-fried salmon glazed with soy, honey and ginger, with rice and a quick sweet-sour cucumber salad.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Slice the cucumber thinly and mix it with the vinegar, sugar and a pinch of salt. Keep it in the fridge while you cook.
Mix the soy sauce, honey and grated ginger in a cup.

steps.text: Pat the salmon dry. Heat the oil in a frying pan on medium-high. Fry the salmon for 4 minutes, then turn and fry 4 minutes more.
steps.tip: Start skin side down and do not move it while it cooks, so it gets a golden crust.

steps.text: Turn the heat to low and pour in the sauce. Let it bubble for 1 minute, spooning it over the fish, until sticky and glazed.
steps.tip: Honey burns quickly, so keep the heat low and keep spooning.

steps: Toast the sesame seeds in a dry pan for a moment if you like. Serve the salmon on the rice with the sauce from the pan, the cucumber salad on the side and sesame on top.

title: Korean-style beef rice bowls
description: Quick bulgogi-style minced beef with soy, honey, garlic and sesame, over rice with crunchy vegetables.
steps: Cook the rice. Cut the carrot and cucumber into matchsticks.
Brown the beef in a hot pan, breaking it up, for 6 minutes. Pour off excess fat.
Add the garlic, ginger, soy sauce, honey and chili and cook 3 minutes until sticky. Stir in the sesame oil.
Serve on rice with the vegetables, spring onion and sesame.

title: Vegetable bibimbap with fried egg
description: Korean rice bowl with sesame spinach, carrot, zucchini and mushrooms, a fried egg and a spicy sauce.
steps: Cook the rice. Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze dry and mix with half the sesame oil, garlic and a dash of soy.
Fry the carrot strips, zucchini strips and sliced mushrooms separately in a little oil, seasoning each with soy. Cook the edamame.
Fry the eggs so the yolks stay runny.
Put rice in bowls, arrange the vegetables on top with an egg, and serve with the chili sauce, the rest of the sesame oil and sesame seeds.

title: Chana masala
description: North Indian chickpea curry with tomato, ginger and warm spices. Vegan and even better the next day.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {500 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat until you serve.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Chop the onions finely. Grate or finely chop the garlic and ginger. Drain and rinse the chickpeas.

steps.text: Heat the sunflower oil in a large pan on medium heat. Fry the onions for 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and golden brown.
steps.tip: Golden onions give the sauce its sweet, deep taste. If they stick, add a spoon of water and scrape the pan.

steps.text: Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, cumin and turmeric and stir for 1 minute until it smells strongly of spice.
steps.tip: Keep stirring so the spices do not burn. If the pan looks dry, add a spoon of water.

steps.text: Add the tomatoes, chickpeas, salt and {200 ml} water. Bring to a bubble and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then. Halfway through, crush a few chickpeas against the side of the pan with your spoon.
steps.tip: The crushed chickpeas thicken the sauce. It is ready when it coats the back of a spoon.

steps: Stir in the spinach a handful at a time until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Squeeze in the lemon juice, taste and add salt if needed. Serve with the rice.

title: Red lentil dal with spinach
description: Creamy red lentils with turmeric, cumin and a little coconut milk. Ready in 30 minutes, costs very little.

steps.text: Rinse the lentils in a sieve until the water runs clear. Start the rice: put it in a pot with {450 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Chop the onion finely, and grate or finely chop the garlic and ginger.
Heat the oil in a large pot on medium heat and fry the onion for 6 minutes until soft and golden at the edges.
Add the garlic, ginger, turmeric, cumin and curry powder and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.text: Add the lentils, tomatoes, coconut milk, salt and {700 ml} water. Bring to the boil, then simmer on low for 20 minutes, stirring every few minutes so it does not stick.
steps.tip: It is ready when the lentils have fallen apart into a thick, soft porridge. Add a splash of water if it gets too thick before then.

steps.text: Stir in the spinach until it wilts, about 2 minutes. Taste and add salt if needed. Serve with the rice.
steps.tip: Dal thickens as it stands. Loosen leftovers with a little water when you reheat them.

title: Chicken tikka-style curry
description: Yogurt-marinated chicken in a mild, creamy tomato curry sauce. A family favourite with rice.

steps.text: Cut the chicken into bite-size cubes. Grate the garlic and ginger. In a bowl mix the yogurt with half the curry powder, the paprika and half the garlic. Add the chicken, stir to coat and leave for 15 minutes.
steps.tip: You can marinate it in the morning or the night before and keep it in the fridge. The yogurt makes the chicken tender.

steps.text: Meanwhile start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps: Chop the onion finely. Heat the oil in a large pan on medium heat and fry the onion for 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the rest of the garlic, the ginger and the rest of the curry powder and stir for 1 minute until fragrant.

steps.text: Add the chicken with all its marinade, turn the heat to medium-high and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until the chicken is white on the outside.
steps.tip: The yogurt may look split at first. That is fine, it comes together in the sauce.

steps.text: Pour in the passata and add the salt. Bring to a bubble, then simmer on low for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the chicken is cooked through and the sauce has thickened.
steps.tip: Cut a large piece in half to check: there should be no pink in the middle.

steps: Stir in the cream and heat for 1 minute without letting it boil. Taste for salt and serve with the rice.

title: Pork and cabbage noodles
description: Chinese-style stir-fried noodles with minced pork, cabbage, carrot, ginger and soy.
steps: Cook the noodles as the packet says and rinse with cold water.
Brown the pork in the oil in a wok for 5 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic.
Add the shredded cabbage and carrot and stir-fry 4 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy and hoisin sauce and toss until hot. Top with spring onion.

title: Thai red curry with tofu
description: Crispy tofu and vegetables in a red curry coconut sauce. Fully plant-based.
steps: Cook the rice. Press the tofu dry, cut into cubes, toss with the cornstarch and fry in the oil until golden. Set aside.
Fry the curry paste for 1 minute, add the coconut milk and 150 ml water.
Add the vegetables and simmer 10 minutes.
Add the tofu, soy sauce and lemon juice and serve with rice.

title: Chicken katsu curry
description: Japanese breaded chicken with a mild curry sauce, rice and shredded cabbage.
steps: Cook the rice. Soften the chopped onion and carrot in 1 tbsp oil for 8 minutes.
Stir in 2 tbsp of the flour and the curry powder, then 500 ml water with the stock cube, the honey and soy. Simmer 15 minutes and blend smooth.
Flatten the chicken, coat in the rest of the flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs, and fry in the rest of the oil 4 minutes a side.
Slice the chicken and serve on rice with the sauce and finely shredded cabbage.

title: Sweet and sour pork
description: Crispy pork pieces with pepper, onion and pineapple in a bright sweet and sour sauce.

steps.text: Start the rice: rinse it, put it in a pot with {550 ml} water and a pinch of salt, bring to the boil, then cover and cook on the lowest heat for 12 minutes. Leave it covered off the heat.
steps.tip: Keeping the lid on is what makes rice fluffy. Do not peek while it cooks.

steps.text: Cut the pork into 2 cm cubes. Beat the egg in a bowl, add the pork and toss, then sprinkle over {3 tbsp} of the cornstarch and mix until every piece is coated.
steps.tip: This coating makes the crisp crust. It looks pasty at first, which is fine.

steps: Cut the peppers and onion into chunks and drain the pineapple. In a cup mix the ketchup, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, the last of the cornstarch and {100 ml} water.

steps.text: Heat {3 tbsp} of the oil in a large frying pan on medium-high. Fry the pork in one layer for about 8 minutes, turning, until golden, crisp and cooked through. Lift it out onto kitchen paper.
steps.tip: Do not crowd the pan or the coating goes soggy. Fry in two batches if needed.

steps: Wipe out any burnt bits, add the rest of the oil and stir-fry the peppers and onion for 3 minutes so they stay a little crunchy. Add the pineapple.

steps.text: Stir the sauce, pour it in and let it bubble for 1 to 2 minutes until thick and glossy. Toss the pork through just before serving with the rice.
steps.tip: Adding the pork at the last moment keeps it crisp.
